items.title: Clearing up a robot’s fuzzy memory
items.summary: The system identifies entries in a robot’s memory that might be wrong and corrects the descriptions of mislabeled objects. Called UQ-DAAAM (which stands for Uncertainty Quantification for Describe Anything, Anywhere, at Any Moment), the system compares multiple descriptions of the same object, seen from different viewpoints, to quantify the robot’s uncertainty about what it saw.

items.title: Wave Physics as Representation: Tensor-Structured Neural Reconstruction for Ocean Acoustic Fields
items.summary: Reconstructing three-dimensional (3D) complex ocean acoustic fields from sparse measurements is challenging due to highly oscillatory wave structures and restricted sensing patterns/routes. This work takes an alternative route: instead of solving a fully specified wave equation, it extracts a structured representation from wave physics and learns its components from data.

items.title: MuLaCover: Flexible Cover Song Generation via Symbolic Tonal Control
items.summary: A cover song re-renders an existing piece, most commonly by preserving its tonal content -- melody and chord progression -- while reshaping other musical attributes. This suggests a natural formulation for generative cover synthesis with pretrained music language models: explicitly control tonal content, while specifying lyrics and style through text.

items.title: OLIVE: View-Augmented Latent Prediction with Waveform Reconstruction for Speech SSL
items.summary: We propose Online Latent prediction with Invariant Views and rEconstruction (OLIVE), a self-supervised speech representation learning framework that jointly optimizes analysis and synthesis objectives. Adding reconstruction largely preserves the speech recognition performance of masked latent prediction alone, while improving waveform reconstruction and speaker tasks.

items.title: DUET: Unified Dual-Space Emotion Control for Diffusion and Flow-Matching Driven Text-to-Speech
items.summary: Diffusion and flow-matching based text-to-speech (TTS) models excel in naturalness but often lack explicit emotion control, as emotional signals remain entangled with speaker identity. This inspires a plug-and-play framework DUET for emotion control over pretrained diffusion and flow-matching based TTS models.

items.title: ENACT-Heart -- ENsemble-based Assessment Using CNN and Transformer on Heart Sounds
items.summary: ENACT-Heart is a two-branch ensemble for heart-sound classification. A Vision Transformer (ViT) processes spectrogram images, while a convolutional neural network (CNN) processes visualizations of waveforms and spectral centroids derived from the same recordings. On the PASCAL heart-sound dataset, the ensemble achieved an accuracy of 97.52%, compared with 93.88% for the ViT and 95.45% for the CNN.

items.title: PAID: Phoneme-Aligned Acoustic Units for Cross-Corpus L1-Background Classification
items.summary: First-language (L1) background classification from second-language English speech aims to identify pronunciation-related acoustic cues that remain informative across speakers and corpora. Global pooling is commonly used to aggregate frame-level speech representations, but averaging features across an utterance may obscure local acoustic differences in how individual phonemes are pronounced.

items.title: SAUCE: Summary Analysis Using Conversation Entailment
items.summary: With the growing need for evaluating Large Language Models (LLMs) and their applications to speech, challenges persist in summarizing and evaluating conversations that lack a clear end goal. It measures the accuracy and the fact coverage of a summary through the entailment between conversation and text.

items.title: SonoDyno: A Sonic Dynamometer for Engine Speed and Load Estimation from Audio
items.summary: Controllable engine sound synthesis, Active Sound Design and engine order analysis all build on the relationship between the sound of an engine and its momentary operating state: its speed and its load.

items.title: Human-like cross-language generalisation in deep neural speaker embeddings and its acoustic foundations
items.summary: Generalisability is a central question for deep neural networks, including the cross-language generalisation of speaker embeddings. This study examined whether deep neural speaker embeddings generalise across languages and how such generalisation relates to human perception and acoustic structure.

items.title: The Hearpiece Database of Binaural Room Impulse Responses and Driver Responses on KEMAR
items.summary: This document describes the measurement setup, signal processing, data organization, and MATLAB file format of a database of acoustic responses measured on a Knowles Electronics Manikin for Acoustic Research (KEMAR) using the Hearpiece, a multi-microphone, multi-driver in-ear research device.

items.title: Speaker-Consistent Grounding for Confusion-Resilient LLM-Based Target Speech Extraction
items.summary: Deterministic target-speaker extraction (TSE) tends to preserve observed linguistic content but may extract the interfering speaker. In contrast, autoregressive generative TSE improves perceptual quality, but is prone to content hallucination and speaker identity drift, which can be mitigated by model grounding with the evidence from the deterministic TSE.

items.title: Virtual Microphone Array for Direction-of-Arrival Estimation Based on Fiber-Optic Position Sensing
items.summary: This paper presents a virtual microphone array approach for estimating the direction of arrival of a sound source using a moving microphone and a stationary reference microphone. The method exploits the microphone motion to generate a time-varying array geometry, using fiber-optic position sensing to reconstruct the trajectory and determine the resulting virtual microphone configurations.

items.title: CLRM: Cross-Layer Relation Modeling for Audio Deepfake Detection
items.summary: Audio deepfake detection (ADD) aims to distinguish bonafide speech from synthetic or manipulated speech. We propose Cross-Layer Relation Modeling (\ours{}), which explicitly encodes cross-layer relations alongside layer-specific features, making both directly available for ADD. These findings support explicit cross-layer comparisons as useful detection inputs for SSL-based audio deepfake detectors.

items.title: Does RRT* Work on Uneven Terrain Meshes?
items.summary: The optimal rapidly exploring random tree (RRT*) is proven asymptotically optimal on open subsets of Euclidean space with straight-line local planning. First, the original RRT* cannot run on a mesh: the surface has zero volume, so uniform sampling never hits it, no clearance ball fits in it, and chords across a fold leave it.

items.title: Time-to-Goal: Learned Temporal Metrics for Long-Horizon Planning with JEPA World Models
items.summary: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) support planning by comparing predicted latent states with an encoded goal. We examine this mismatch in flat LeWorldModel (LeWM) by analyzing how its Euclidean goal cost changes with temporal separation. These results show that learning temporal ordering for the goal cost can substantially improve latent planning even with a flat world model.

items.title: RACE: Calibrated Cumulative Scoring for Rollout-Free Robot Policy Checkpoint Selection
items.summary: Assessing the deployment performance of learned robot policies during training is challenging, as directly measuring task success requires costly real-world trials for each candidate checkpoint. Averaged validation loss offers a rollout-free alternative, but its checkpoint rankings can be inconsistent with deployment performance.

items.title: ZipDrift: Generating Multimodal Short-Horizon MPC Costs with One-Step Drifting Models
items.summary: Short-horizon model predictive control (MPC) is fast but myopic. ZipMPC compensates by learning a context-dependent correction of the short-horizon cost that imitates a long-horizon expert.

items.title: Closed-Loop Adaptive Sampling on a Generative Ocean Model
items.summary: Adaptive sampling can substantially improve the value of sparse ocean observations by directing mobile robots toward measurements that are most informative for an evolving environment.

items.title: GRASP: Gradient-Guided Sampling for Contact-Rich Physics-Based Motion Retargeting
items.summary: We study physics-based retargeting of human demonstrations for robot learning: finding robot controls that reproduce reference motions under contact dynamics. We propose GRASP (Gradient Recovery from Archived Samples for Proposals), which combines sampling-based exploration with gradient-guided refinement without requiring a differentiable simulator.

items.title: OUCH: Objective, Uniform, Controlled Haptic Stimulation for Automated Neurological Assessment
items.summary: Motor responses evoked by noxious stimulation are used to assess neurological function in hospitalized patients with disorders of consciousness. Here, we present OUCH (Objective, Uniform, Controlled Haptic stimulation), a wrist-worn device that uses pneumatic actuation to deliver noxious mechanical stimuli.

items.title: OdorSpaces: Visual-Olfactory Embodied Navigation in 3D Environments
items.summary: Olfaction provides critical information about airborne chemical cues, yet it remains largely underexplored in embodied AI, with limited prior machine olfaction work focusing primarily on semantic odor perception. We introduce OdorSpaces, a physics-based simulation platform and benchmark for visual-olfactory embodied navigation.

items.title: Correct Robots Before They Make Mistakes: Proactive Human-in-the-Loop Intervention via Preference Learning
items.summary: This paper presents Proactive Human-in-the-Loop (PHIL), a framework for proactive policy correction and preference-based post-training. PHIL pairs rejected policy predictions with corrective action chunks subsequently executed from the same physical state over the same horizon, and preference-based post-training encourages the policy to favor these corrections.

items.title: $\mathcal{C}^\infty$ Smooth Trajectory Planning with Application to Soft Robots
items.summary: High motion performance and avoiding structural vibrations rely on smooth trajectory planning. Although unknown for soft continuum robots, the exact smoothness requirement can potentially be much larger than previously considered ones such as $\mathbf{\mathcal{C}^4}$ for collaborative robots and $\mathbf{\mathcal{C}^5}$ for quadcopter drones.

items.title: Contact-Implicit Whole-Body Trajectory Optimization for Dynamic Humanoid Locomotion on Parameterizable Uneven Terrain
items.summary: This letter presents a trajectory planner for humanoid robots to perform dynamic motions on complex, parameterizable terrains using a contact-implicit whole-body optimization framework. To plan bipedal locomotion on steps, ramps, and other terrains, we propose a mathematical model to approximate ground geometry with a smooth surface.

items.title: ELA: End-to-End Latent Action Policy Learning from Video Demonstrations
items.summary: Robot imitation learning is limited by the scarcity of action-labeled data, while action-free demonstrations such as videos are abundant. This paper introduces ELA, an end-to-end framework for learning from video demonstrations via latent actions jointly optimized for policy learning and action decoding.

items.title: MESA: An Evaluation Framework for Compositional, Semantic, and Spatial Generalization in Robotics
items.summary: We introduce MESA, an evaluation framework designed for precise, reproducible measurement of language-conditioned policy generalization.

items.title: Ctrl-F: Force as an Interface for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
items.summary: Humanoid motion tracking has scaled to general policies that reproduce diverse human motion, but the resulting behavior is in free-space: the tracker knows where the body should be, not how it should interact with the environment. We argue that force is a natural command channel between motion imitation and object interaction, one that specifies not just where to make contact but how hard.

items.title: Jev with Foresight: Safe Language-Guided Autonomous Driving via a Language World Model
items.summary: Large language models understand passengers' driving commands, but as driving agents they reason in generated text for seconds and must infer each action's consequences implicitly from the scene.

items.title: BrainBind: Bridging Synchronized EEG and fMRI through Long-Form Naturalistic Video Representations
items.summary: Real-world vision is dynamic and scene-rich, while EEG and fMRI resolve it at complementary temporal and spatial scales. We study the synchronized case: EEG and fMRI are recorded during the same long-form naturalistic viewing, giving a shared stimulus but also recurring narrative context and many semantically similar candidates.

items.title: AGORA: Reliability-Aware Aggregation of LLM Judges via Item-Response Theory
items.summary: LLM-as-a-judge is a common substitute for costly human evaluation, and aggregating several judges is the standard remedy for any single judge's bias. Judge pools mix judges of very different reliability, while the human-labeled sets that validate them hold a few hundred items or fewer.

items.title: VirtualTrialHarness: Coordinating Agentic Operationalization of Virtual Trial Protocols Across Complex Clinical Schemas
items.summary: Virtual trials use routinely collected clinical data to evaluate treatment strategies, but translating a study protocol into an executable analysis requires determining how clinical concepts and study requirements should be represented in the available data and applied consistently across the workflow.

items.title: Whose Transparency is it Anyway? Understanding Generative AI Transparency Needs and Gaps Across Stakeholders
items.summary: Transparency has become a central principle in AI governance, yet there is little agreement about what transparency means, for whom, and in what contexts.

items.title: Iterated creation, grading, and revision of data science projects by language models
items.summary: We evaluate the extent to which agentic AI models can complete an end-to-end data science project, and how this improves with feedback. By writer the extent of the increase ranges from 3 percentage points for Anthropic's Opus 5.5 to 46 percentage points for Anthropic's Haiku 4.5, and by grader it ranges from 13 percentage points for Google's Gemini 3.8 Flash to 32 percentage points for Anthropic's Haiku 4.5.

items.title: Towards Efficient Whole Page Ranking with One-Pass Inference
items.summary: Whole-page ranking jointly optimizes advertisements and organic content to balance business outcomes and user engagement under complex layout and business constraints. Existing non-autoregressive (NAR) approaches enable efficient page generation but typically score candidate items independently of previously selected items, limiting their ability to capture order-dependent interactions.

items.title: MA-SafeDiffuser: Safe Multi-Agent Planning with Diffusion Probabilistic Models
items.summary: We propose MA-SafeDiffuser, a multi-agent extension of SafeDiffuser that equips diffusion-based trajectory planners with finite-time diffusion invariance guarantees for joint-agent safety specifications. Empirically, MA-SafeDiffuser reduces violation counts relative to unconstrained diffusion baselines, while retaining planning quality. We provide algorithms, proofs, and reference implementations.

items.title: SlackBench: Benchmarking Agents on Collaborative Projects Grounded in Real Code Repositories
items.summary: Yet existing benchmarks fall short of real knowledge work: many rely on synthetic data or isolated tasks, missing the complex, multi-party dynamics of collaborative projects, where critical information is scattered across conversations, code, and evolving decisions.

items.title: Can Large Language Models Review the Scientific Literature? A Test Against a 102-Article Benchmark
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support scientific literature reviews, yet evaluations often examine individual tasks rather than the review process as a whole. The benchmark is a published review of the Spanish plume weather pattern and its 102-article corpus.

items.title: Towards Robust Long-Lived Agents: Benchmarking Experience Lifecycles in Evolving Environments
items.summary: Such assistance requires agents to discover how unfamiliar environments work, reuse what they learn across tasks, and keep that experience current as environments evolve. Existing benchmarks increasingly study experience reuse and adaptation, but provide limited insight into which parts of accumulated experience agents revise, retain, or lose.

items.title: A Feasibility Condition for Confidence-Gated Tiered LLM Inference
items.summary: Tiered inference distributes large language model computation across a hierarchy of devices, from on-device and edge hardware to the datacenter, and is increasingly offered as the route to cheaper, lower-latency, and more private serving.

items.title: Challenge-Aware Knowledge Recruitment with Meta-Agent Supervision for Medical Multi-Agent Reasoning
items.summary: Large language models perform strongly on standard medical QA but degrade on harder reasoning tasks, where multi-agent debate often fails to beat strong single-model prompting. We propose challenge-aware adaptive recruitment: an external CHALLENGER inspects the evolving reasoning trace and identifies specific factual or expertise gaps.

items.title: Uncertainty-Aware Resource Orchestration for Agentic AI Systems
items.summary: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems powered by large language models (LLMs) execute as autonomous multi-step pipelines that dynamically invoke tools, integrate observations into memory, and iterate until a task is resolved or a resource budget is exhausted.

items.title: Agent Harness Awareness: Turning Verified Telemetry into Operational Control for Tool-Using Agents
items.summary: Tool descriptions tell an agent what an action can do, but they do not necessarily reveal whether that action is healthy or suitable at the moment of use. We introduce Agent Harness Awareness, a trust-separated design in which the host supplies a small, fresh, verified state snapshot before a consequential action while retaining measurement, enforcement, evaluation, and final dispatch authority.

items.title: Who May Overrule the Agent? Evidence-Gated Authority in LLM Review Institutions
items.summary: Multi-agent language-model systems often add a reviewer to improve an upstream agent's decision. We study this as a problem of institutional jurisdiction: conditional on the same proposal, task information, model, and review output, when is the reviewer authorized to make its recommendation binding?
